previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, stage V chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis, hemolytic anemia, and type 2 diabetes, was admitted with fever, lethargy, and urinary incontinence. He was diagnosed with a urinary tract infection based on urinalysis showing white blood cells and bacteria, despite negative and contaminated urine cultures. He was treated with a seven-day course of IV cefepime and received two units of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia. Conjunctivitis was treated with a five-day course of topical erythromycin. His pomalidomide was held during infection and resumed at discharge. He completed dialysis during admission and was stabilized medically. He improved clinically, with resolution of fever and mental status changes, and was discharged to extended care rehab with plans for follow-up on blood counts, electrolytes, and oncology care.

LOWER CHEST: Trace bilateral pleural effusions.  Bibasilar opacities may be

Moderate cardiomegaly with trace pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogeneous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced
scan.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary
dilatation.  The gallbladder contains numerous tiny layering gallstones,

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced scan.  There is no
pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen is moderately enlarged, measuring up to 16.9 cm (02:27). 
The spleen shows normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of focal
lesions.  A small accessory spleen is again noted at the splenic hilum.

ADRENALS: The right adrenal gland is normal in size and shape. Left adrenal

normal caliber and wall thickness throughout.  Moderate circumferential wall
thickening involving the rectum is likely compatible with colitis.  Colonic

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The prostate and seminal vesicles are normal.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

disease is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
The bones again appear diffusely demineralized, similar appearance to prior

SOFT TISSUES: An umbilical hernia containing fat is noted. Gynecomastia is
